title: Week 8 Analysis
subtitle: Cadegn goes perfect in the AFC South and takes back first by 19.
intro_paragraphs: Five of the eight divisions changed order this week, and Cadegn gained 30 points to reach 76, the highest total anyone has had this season. The AFC South and AFC West moved Cadegn's way, and the lead over second place is now 19, the biggest since Week 4. Dustin jumped from a tie for 5th to 2nd. Hume, last week's leader, lost 4 and dropped to 6th.
New Orleans, the Giants, San Francisco, and Houston had their byes this week. They've played seven games, along with the ten teams that had earlier byes. Everyone else has played eight.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn's Second Perfect Division
fun_facts.body: Houston didn't play, and still moved from third to second in the AFC South when the Colts fell to 2-6. That finished off Cadegn's pick exactly: Jaguars, Texans, Colts, Titans. The division went from 6 points to 25, and it's the first perfect division anyone has had outside the AFC East since Cadegn's NFC East broke last week. Cadegn also picked up 9 from the Broncos and Chiefs going 1-2 in the AFC West and 5 in the NFC South when the Falcons moved into third, which also completed the bottom-2 bonus. The only loss was 3 in the NFC East. Net: +30, tied with Tom's Week 2 for the fourth-biggest week of the season, behind Dilger's +46 and Hume's +45 in Week 2 and Cadegn's own +39 in Week 4.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn Leads Again
fun_facts.body: One week after losing first place, Cadegn has it back with the most perfect divisions (2), the most top-2 bonuses (3), the most bottom-2 bonuses (3), and the most exact hits (15 of 32). Cadegn also has 4 of 8 division-winner picks currently right after the Broncos took over the AFC West, the most in the pool. Cadegn has now led in four of the eight weeks.

fun_facts.heading: Dustin Climbs to 2nd
fun_facts.body: Dustin gained 20, the second-best week in the pool this week. The AFC West was worth 9: Broncos first, Chiefs second, plus the top-2 bonus. The Buccaneers and Falcons moving into second and third in the NFC South added 6, the AFC South added 5, and the Bengals in second in the AFC North added 3. The only loss was 3 in the NFC East when Washington passed Philadelphia. Dustin was tied for 5th and 12 back last week, and is now alone in 2nd at 57.

fun_facts.heading: A Three-Way Tie for 3rd
fun_facts.body: Mike T, Dilger, and Tom are all at 48, and they match on all four tiebreakers: one perfect division, one top-2 bonus, two bottom-2 bonuses, and 11 exact hits each. With the point-total tiebreaker still not set up, they're officially tied for 3rd. They got there differently. Dilger gained 11 with no losses. Tom gained 5. Mike T gained only 2, because the Broncos passing the Chiefs wiped out all 9 of Mike T's AFC West points.

fun_facts.heading: Hume Falls to 6th
fun_facts.body: Hume had the same AFC West problem: picking the Chiefs first and the Broncos second was worth 9 last week and nothing this week. The NFC East cost another 3. The AFC South (+5) and NFC South (+3) couldn't cover it, and Hume went from 1st at 49 to 6th at 45, 31 behind the lead.

fun_facts.heading: Farmer Gives It Back
fun_facts.body: Last week the NFC East was worth 8 to Farmer: the Eagles in third, the Commanders in last, and the bottom-2 bonus. This week Washington tied and Philadelphia lost, the two swapped places, and all 8 points went away. The NFC South cost 3 more. The AFC South (+6, including the top-2 bonus for Jaguars-Texans) and the Broncos (+3) kept it to -2. Farmer is last at 33, 12 behind Hume, and still the only bettor without a perfect division.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC North Finally Pays
fun_facts.body: The Steelers moved into first at 6-2, the Bengals are second at 5-2, the Browns dropped to third, and the Ravens are still last at 4-4. For the first time since Week 5, somebody scored there: Mike T, Dustin, and Tom picked the Bengals second and got 3 each. Nobody picked the Steelers to win the division, so all seven division-winner picks there are still wrong.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks: Still Three
fun_facts.body: The Bills first, the Patriots second, and the Cardinals last are still holding, 3 of the 8 preseason unanimous picks. The pool's unanimous pick for last in the AFC West, the Raiders, are third at 4-4. The team in last is the Chargers, who are 0-7. The Rams, the unanimous pick to win the NFC West, are 4-4 and behind the 6-1 49ers, and the Lions, the unanimous pick in the NFC North, are 5-2 and third behind the 6-1 Vikings and 6-2 Bears.

closing_paragraph: Cadegn leads by 19, and everyone from 2nd to 6th is within 12 of each other. The AFC West and AFC North both changed leaders this week, and the NFC South has three teams at 3-4 or 3-5, so there's still plenty that can move. Same time next Tuesday.
